column1: Across the whole vending machine, an operation that is illegal for the machine's current condition results in an InvalidMachineStateException rather than a printed message and a normal return. Which practical benefit does that give the code that CALLS these operations?,It makes the code run faster because no string is printed,The caller cannot accidentally carry on as if the operation had succeeded - a failed call interrupts the flow instead of returning normally and leaving the caller to guess,It guarantees the machine will never end up in a wrong condition,It removes the need for the caller to handle any errors,,2,"Main relies on exactly this: it wraps the deliberately-illegal calls in try/catch and prints 'Expected failure: ...'. If those calls had returned silently, Main could not have told the difference between a rejection and a success.",1
